title: Competition among Aedes aegypti larvae in microcosms
author: Kurt Steinwascher
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.tcweixe
materials: Continue until all larvae have pupated or died.

steps.title: Obtain mosquito eggs
steps.instruction: Obtain Aedes aegypti eggs from the colony after feeding females on a mouse.

steps.title: Hatch eggs in water
steps.instruction: Place the eggs in distilled water and immerse for at least 2 hours.

steps.title: Assign random treatment numbers (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Create 20 treatment combinations (4 food levels × 5 densities) and assign a random number to each; prepare 5 replicates per treatment.

steps.title: Label and number vials (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Number 100 flat‑bottomed shell vials (25 mm diameter × 95 mm tall) with the random treatment number.

steps.title: Add water to vials (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Add 20 ml distilled water to each vial.

steps.title: Prepare yeast solutions (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Weigh baker’s yeast and dissolve in distilled water to give per‑larva concentrations of 2, 3, 4, 5 mg yeast. For each density (4‑8 larvae per vial) calculate total yeast (e.g., 2 mg × 4 = 8 mg) and dissolve that amount in 0.5 ml distilled water; add the 0.5 ml to the 20 ml water in the appropriate vials. Prepare 5 replicates of each of the 20 treatments.

steps.title: Add larvae to vials (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Count 4, 5, 6, 7 or 8 larvae into each vial according to its treatment label.

steps.title: Arrange and cover vials (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Arrange vials in numerical order (randomized sequence) and cover each with cheese cloth to prevent food or other mosquitoes from entering.

steps.title: Store vials (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Place vials in a room at ambient Florida temperatures ranging from 18 °C to 33 °C.

steps.title: Monitor for pupation (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Designate the day the experiment starts as day 0; beginning on day 4 (the day before expected pupation) inspect each vial for pupae.

steps.title: Transfer pupae to holding vials (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Using a fire‑polished wide‑mouth glass pipette (~2 mm diameter), capture each pupa at the water surface, gently blow it into a holding shell vial containing 10 ml distilled water, record the original vial number, treatment, and date, and place only one pupa per holding vial.

substeps.instruction: Capture pupa with fire‑polished pipette (~2 mm diameter)
Gently blow pupa into holding vial with 10 ml distilled water
Record original vial number, treatment, and date of pupation
Place only one pupa per holding vial

steps.title: Weigh and sex pupae (Exp 1)
steps.instruction: Remove the pupa from the holding vial with a pipette, blot it on a paper towel, pick it up with fine‑tipped forceps, weigh on a balance to the nearest 0.01 mg and record the weight, examine under a 10× stereoscopic microscope to determine sex and record it, then return the pupa to a water vial to complete pupation.

substeps.instruction: Blot pupa on paper towel and pick up with fine‑tipped forceps
Weigh to the nearest 0.01 mg and record weight
Determine sex under a 10× stereoscopic microscope and record sex
Return pupa to a vial of water to complete pupation

steps.title: Assign random treatment numbers (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Create 4 treatment combinations (2 food levels × 2 densities) and assign a random number to each; prepare 40 replicates per treatment.

steps.title: Label and number vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Number 160 flat‑bottomed shell vials (25 mm diameter × 95 mm tall) with the random treatment number.

steps.title: Add water to vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Add 20 ml distilled water to each vial.

steps.title: Prepare yeast solutions (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Weigh baker’s yeast and dissolve in distilled water to give per‑larva concentrations of 3 mg and 4 mg. For each density (5 or 6 larvae per vial) calculate total yeast (e.g., 3 mg × 5 = 15 mg) and dissolve that amount in 0.5 ml distilled water; add the 0.5 ml to the 20 ml water in the appropriate vials. Prepare 40 replicates of each of the 4 treatments.

steps.title: Add larvae to vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Count 5 or 6 larvae into each vial according to its treatment label.

steps.title: Arrange and cover vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Arrange vials in numerical order (randomized sequence) and cover each with cheese cloth.

steps.title: Store vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Place vials in an insectary at 26 °C with a 12 h light / 12 h dark cycle for the first four days and overnight thereafter.

steps.title: Monitor for pupation (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Designate day 0 as the start; beginning on day 4 inspect vials for pupae.

steps.title: Transfer pupae to holding vials (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Using a fire‑polished wide‑mouth glass pipette (~2 mm diameter), capture each pupa at the water surface, gently blow it into a holding shell vial containing 10 ml distilled water, record the original vial number, treatment, and date, and place only one pupa per holding vial.

Gently blow pupa into holding vial with 10 ml distilled water

steps.title: Weigh and sex pupae (Exp 2)
steps.instruction: Remove the pupa from the holding vial with a pipette, blot it on a paper towel, pick it up with fine‑tipped forceps, weigh on a balance to the nearest 0.01 mg and record the weight, examine under a 10× stereoscopic microscope to determine sex and record it, then return the pupa to a water vial to complete pupation.
